CEREMONIAL MATTERS Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation declaring the week of
  November 10-16, 2025 as Veterans Appreciation Week in the City
  of Pasadena, hie expressed immense gratitude for the contributions
  and sacrifices made by veterans and their families. Koko Panossian,
  Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Director, introduced
  Sarah Town-di Cicco, Pasadena Veterans' Day Planning Committee
  Member, who extended gratitude to the City Council for the
  recognition, spoke on the importance of recognizing those who have
  bravely fought for the country, and shared details for the upcoming
  Veterans' Day event at Centennial Square on November 11, 2025.

  Councilmember Hampton requested for the meeting to be adjourned
  in memory of local dance instructor, Janina Garraway. He spoke on
  her vibrant impacts and serving the community through the joy of
  dancing.

SEPARATELY  CITYWIDE TREE PLANTING FOR AN AMOUNT NOT-TO-

  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the action proposed in the agenda report is not a
  "project" subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines Section 21065 and within the

  (2) Award contract to the lowest responsive and best bid dated
  September 22, 2025, submitted by United Pacific Services Inc., in
  response to specifications for Citywide tree planting, authorize the

Council Minutes  6  11/10/2025
   City Manager to enter into a contract for an amount not-to-exceed
  $297,000 which includes the base contract amount of $270,000 and
  a contingency of $27,000 to provide for potential change orders.
n  (Contract No. 33455)

  Mike Polka, Pasadena resident, expressed his concerns
  regarding the City's approach to tree planting, including the
  budget and planting schedule.

  In response to Councilmember Hampton's inquiry regarding the
  City's tree planting schedule, Michael King, Forestry Program
  Coordinator, reported that the City's planting season typically starts
  in the fall and concludes by the end of spring. He noted that there
  were delays earlier this year, which led to planting work concluding
  in June before experiencing heat waves.

  In response to Councilmember Cole's inquiry regarding the
  responsibility of contractors to replace trees that died just after
  planting, Forestry Program Coordinator King reported that City staff
  will review the terms of the current contract for tree replacement
  provisions and ensure the contractors meet their obligations under
  the contract. In response to Mayor Gordo's inquiry regarding the
  performance standards in the contract, Forestry Program
  Coordinator King stated that the current contract specifications state
  that the planting and installation contractor is responsible for
  maintaining the health and conditions of the trees until September.
)
  Mayor Gordo and Councilmember Cole advocated for the City to
  pursue the contractor's responsibilities in terms of performance
  standards and quality assurance.

  MOTION:  It was moved by Councilmember Hampton, seconded by
  Councilmember Masuda, to approve the staff recommendation.
  (Motion unanimously approved) (Absent: None)

RECOMMENDATIONS  CONSIDERATION OF A CALL FOR REVIEW OF THE BOARD OF
FROM OFFICERS AND  ZONING APPEALS DECISION TO THE CITY COUNCIL
DEPARTMENTS  REGARDING HILLSIDE DEVELOPMENT PERMIT NO. 7134, TO
  ALLOW A NEW 4,280 SQUARE-FOOT, TWO-STORY SINGLE-
City Council  FAMILY DWELLING WITH AN ATTACHED 2,685 SQUARE-FOOT
  SIX-CAR GARAGE, FOR THE PROPERTY LOCATED AT 1530
  SCENIC DRIVE (Councilmember Madison)

  Councilmember Madison provided a brief overview of the item and
  his decision to call for review.

  Councilmember Cole noted that the Board of Zoning Appeals voted
  unanimously on the matter and expressed concerns that having the
  City Council review the matter due to disagreement with the Board's
  decision may potentially preclude the need of having a Board of
  Zoning Appeals. Vice Mayor Rivas echoed similar sentiments and
  expressed concerns regarding the efficient use of City staff time and
  resources for a process that appears to be non-controversial.

  Mayor Gordo noted that a group of residents have already appealed
  the decision, which obligates the City Council to revisit Board of
  Zoning Appeals' decision. Councilmember Madison's request is also
  consistent with the City's Municipal Code and the appeal process.

  Councilmembers Hampton and Jones expressed support for the call
  for review and for the City Council to hear the residents' concerns.

  MOTION:  It was moved by Councilmember Madison, seconded by
  Councilmember Jones, to approve the call for review request.
